title: Menu scrolling feels unresponsive: measure whether it is the scroll step, wheel event handling or the per-frame text rebuild
description:
User report 2026-10-03 on VIEW-12's model menu: wheel scrolling of the scroll boxes does not feel responsive, though the scene seems to hold 60 fps. Suspects, to be measured rather than guessed: (1) the step: MenuScrollBox scrolls SCROLL_SPEED times a wheel delta scaled by Clock.deltaTime() (frame-time scaled, so the distance per notch varies with frame time) and is then rounded to whole rows for drawing, so small steps may produce no visible movement; (2) wheel events are queued and drained once per frame (queuedMouseWheelTicks, SCROLL_DECAY_MS), adding latency or dropping ticks; (3) SceneModelMenu rebuilds both boxes' HyperStrings and re-lays them out every frame. Instrument per-notch scroll distance, event-to-frame latency and menu draw time, report them, then fix the cause: for example a fixed rows-per-notch step independent of frame time, and caching the laid-out text until rows or width change.

Rework 2026-10-03 (user): the list must be able to rest between rows and scroll smoothly. Remove the whole-row rounding of the drawn offset (MenuScrollBox.drawnScrollOffsetY, added in VIEW-12 to keep a half row out from under the MODELS title) and instead clip each box's rows to the box's own rectangle, so a partly scrolled row is cut by the box edge and never drawn under a title. A wheel notch moves a target offset by ROWS_PER_WHEEL_NOTCH rows; the drawn offset eases toward the target over about 120 ms (frame-time independent, exact accumulation, no dropped ticks as already fixed). Click and hover bounds follow the drawn offset, including a half-visible row. Centring the current model on open may land between rows.

Rework 3, 2026-10-03 (user, on a trackpad): scrolling must be continuous like a normal scroll box, not stepped in increments. The earlier framing ('one notch moves a fixed number of rows') assumed a mouse wheel and was wrong for the user's input device. Root cause, found but left unfixed in the first round: MouseTrap.scrollCallback turns each delta into whole ticks with (int)(4*y) and discards the remainder, so slow trackpad scrolling (many deltas of about 0.05 to 0.2) produces zero ticks and nothing moves for whole swipes. Fix: carry the raw float scroll delta, never truncated, from the GLFW callback to the region under the cursor; the menu box scrolls by delta times a pixels-per-unit constant immediately, so it moves in proportion to the finger and can stop anywhere; the step for a mouse wheel follows from its larger deltas (about one row-scale step per 1.0). Remove the integer tick path from the menu (onWheelTicks, ROWS_PER_WHEEL_NOTCH); keep easing only if it helps coarse wheel deltas and never delays trackpad deltas. Camera zoom keeps its per-unit rate but accumulates fractional deltas instead of dropping them. The region interface VIEW-16's encapsulation rework will generalise must carry this float delta.
definition-of-done:
1. Measurements before and after on the ticket (pixels per notch, latency, menu draw ms). 2. One wheel notch always moves the list a fixed, visible amount (for example 3 rows). 3. Menu draw time does not grow with frame-by-frame rebuilds (cached layout), or the measurement shows it does not matter. 4. No regression in wrapping, centring or clicks.

7. After a notch the drawn offset passes through intermediate values over several frames and settles exactly on target (logged offsets in a test or through ui-state). 8. A scroll can rest at a non-multiple of the row height; the partly visible top row is clipped at the box edge and nothing is drawn under the MODELS title (screenshot). 9. Clicking the visible part of a half-cut row loads that model.

10. Injected trackpad-sized deltas (for example 50 events of 0.05) move the list proportionally (total equal to 50 x 0.05 x pixels-per-unit within rounding) with visible motion from the first events; no delta is truncated anywhere on the path (unit test on the callback). 11. A slow zoom with small deltas also changes the camera distance. 12. Mouse-wheel-sized deltas (1.0) still give a sensible step. Test with fractional deltas through the automation scroll route (extend it to accept fractional y if needed).
testing-plan: 1. Timing logs around SceneModelMenu.draw. 2. Automation: inject N wheel ticks, read the box offset after each. 3. F5 feel check by the user.
changes-made:
Measured in ring-tool (headless, frames ~20 ms apart; model menu open, cursor on the models box, notches injected through `ixdar-cli scroll` / POST input/scroll; temporary timing lines since removed).

BEFORE (master 6811a7c5):
- Step per notch: 77-114 px, usually 98-107 px (3.3-3.8 rows), spread over 2 frames. Each frame the box moved 1200 x Clock.deltaTime() px = 49-55 px. Clock.deltaTime() spans two frame intervals (~41 ms at 20 ms frames). The claimer never emptied the wheel queue, so onScroll ran again every frame until SCROLL_DECAY_MS (60 ms) after the last tick. Distance per notch = (frames inside the 60 ms window) x (2 x frame time) x 1200, so it changes with frame rate and frame phase. Drawn offset jumped 3 or 4 rows depending on rounding (600->540->480, then 493->450->390).
- Ticks merged: only the sign of the queue was used, so 4 notches 5 ms apart moved 247-253 px, against 396 px for 4 separate notches. About 1.5 notches were lost. Ticks older than 60 ms when a frame came (a long frame) were zeroed before anything drained them.
- Latency: first visible change 1 frame after the notch (20-29 ms) in 22/22 notches. Not a cause.
- SceneModelMenu.draw: 0.34-0.64 ms average per frame at steady state (row rebuild 0.15-0.29, layout 0.013-0.07, glyph draw 0.10-0.19), on a ~20 ms frame, so about 2-3 %. Occasional 3-30 ms outliers, mostly in the rebuild window: allocation / GC. The rebuild does no I/O. Conclusion: the per-frame rebuild does not matter for responsiveness, so no layout cache was added (DoD 3, second branch).

FIX:
- OrbitMouseTrap.WheelClaimer gains onWheelTicks(int ticks). paintUpdate hands every queued tick to the claimer under the cursor exactly once, however old, then empties the queue. The decay and zoom path below it is unchanged. The frame-time-scaled onScroll is a no-op default for claimers.
- MenuScrollBox scrolls ROWS_PER_WHEEL_NOTCH = 3 rows (90 px at 30 px rows) per notch (SCROLL_TICKS_PER_UNIT ticks). It does not read Clock, and the wheel direction is unchanged (toward the user = later rows). SCROLL_SPEED removed.

AFTER (same probe):
- Every notch moves exactly 90.0 px = 3 drawn rows, in a single frame (13/13 single notches, both directions).
- 88 ticks injected, 88 drained, one drain call per notch, |step| always 90 px. A queued 3-notch batch reaches the claimer as one call of -12 ticks (unit test).
- Latency still 1 frame (20-29 ms).
- Menu draw unchanged (0.40-0.51 ms steady).
- Regressions checked live: after 2 notches (offset 600->420), a click on the 5th visible row loaded exactly that model (fixtures/sliver_pinch.dsl; VIEW-14 bounds intact). Reopening the menu centred the current model (offset 285). One notch then drew rows 13.. (offset 375, 3 rows on). The wheel off the menu still zooms by 0.97^4 per notch (3.596 -> 3.184).

Tests: MenuScrollBoxWrapTest.oneWheelNotchMovesThreeWholeRowsAndMergedNotchesAddUp and ScrollRegionHitTest.everyQueuedTickReachesTheClaimerOnceEvenPastTheDecayWindow are new. The latter fails on the old code. Full unit suite: 373 run, 0 failures. mvn -q compile clean. `ixd wt done view-17` passed: synced onto b01a2c5f, 0 diagnostics, build, launch entry 'VIEW-17: ring-tool' ran, screenshots tmp/view17-menu-after-two-notches.png, tmp/view17-menu-centred-then-one-notch.png and tmp/view-17-launch.png.

Side finding, not fixed: GET ui/state returned HTTP 500 on about 2-5 % of polls while the menu was open. The route reads box.text off the render thread while SceneModelMenu.draw replaces it every frame. This only affects automation, not the user.

F5 feel check by the user is still open (testing plan 3).

Rework 2026-10-03 (smooth scrolling, rest between rows). CLIPPING: Camera2D.updateView already sets the GL viewport to the box, and the font shader's ortho projection is the viewport, so every glyph triangle is clipped to the box rectangle by the GL clip volume. That is a real pixel clip and is what InfoPane, ShaderCodePane and Terminal rely on; there is no scissor anywhere in the GL abstraction, and none was needed. Verified live: a row cut at the box top shows a clean horizontal cut 30 px below the top, and nothing of it reaches the MODELS title row. So the half row VIEW-12 rework 3 saw under the title came from the layout of that time (the models box was not yet whole rows tall and placed directly under the title), not from a missing clip; the whole-row rounding added then only hid it. The per-word culling in HyperString.setLineOffsetFromTopRow was lopsided: it culled a word whose row bottom was below the view (wordY < 0), so a part-visible bottom row vanished while a part-visible top row was drawn. Now only rows wholly outside the view are culled (wordY + rowHeight <= 0 or wordY >= height) and a cut row is left to the viewport clip. Shared with InfoPane, Terminal, ShaderCodePane and tooltips, whose part-visible bottom row now also shows, cut at the pane edge.
EASING: MenuScrollBox.scrollOffsetY is the target (whole notches of ROWS_PER_WHEEL_NOTCH = 3 rows added exactly, clamped). drawnScrollOffsetY() eases out cubically from easeStartOffsetY to the target over WHEEL_EASE_NANOS = 120 ms. It is a pure function of the clock (nanoClock, System::nanoTime, swappable by tests), so it does not depend on frame rate or on how often it is sampled, and returns the target exactly once 120 ms have passed. A notch mid-ease restarts the ease from the currently drawn offset toward the new target, so merged or rapid notches add up exactly and none are dropped. Whole-row rounding removed; centring on open sets the target and drawn offset together (no ease) and may land between rows (it lands at 105 px = 3.5 rows in ring-tool). Click and hover bounds are the words' bounds from the draw at the drawn offset, intersected with the box (HyperWord tests viewBounds), so the visible part of a cut row clicks and the part outside the box does not. ui-state reports drawnScrollOffsetY per menu box. maximumScrollOffsetY and the drawnScrollOffsetY name are kept for VIEW-16's scroll bar.

Rework verification (2026-10-03). DoD 7: ring-tool, menu open (Ctrl+I), cursor on the models box, one notch per POST /input/scroll delta -1, ui-state polled about every 20 ms (one frame). Notch 1, frames 28-35: drawn 105.0 -> 120.18 -> 168.15 -> 186.44 -> 190.05 -> 194.63 -> 194.99 -> 195.0 (target 195.0 from the first frame; settles exactly at about 125-145 ms after the request). Notch 2: 195.0 -> 203.8 -> 241.74 -> 262.86 -> 276.84 -> 283.39 -> 284.89 -> 285.0. Logs: tmp/view17-notch-offsets.txt, tmp/view17-notch-offsets-run2-a.txt, tmp/view17-notch-offsets-run2-b.txt. DoD 8: at rest at 285 px (9.5 rows) the top row fixtures/closing_loop_collapse.dsl is cut by a clean line at the box top, with nothing in the MODELS row, and the bottom row neck_armor.dsl is cut at the box bottom above Recompute: tmp/view17-rest-9.5-rows.png, tmp/view17-rest-9.5-rows-top-edge-zoom.png, tmp/view17-rest-9.5-rows-bottom-edge-zoom.png; also centred at 3.5 rows on open: tmp/view17-centred-between-rows.png, tmp/view17-centred-top-edge-zoom.png. DoD 9: a click at window y 22 (the cut-off half, under the title) loaded nothing; a click at y 38 (the visible half) loaded fixtures/closing_loop_collapse.dsl, now highlighted as current: tmp/view17-half-cut-row-clicked-loaded.png. Unit tests (MenuScrollBoxWrapTest): aNotchEasesThroughIntermediateOffsetsAndSettlesExactlyOnTarget, notchesMergedInOneCallOrSpreadMidEaseAddUpExactly, theDrawnOffsetDependsOnTimeNotOnHowManyFramesSampledIt, theBoxRestsBetweenRowsAndAClickOnTheVisiblePartOfACutRowPicksIt (the last fails on the old culling: the bottom cut row was culled); the whole-row rounding test was removed. mvn test 383 run, 0 failures; mvn -q compile clean; tools/teavm-build.sh OK (0 errors); ixd wt done view-17 passed (launch entry ran, tmp/view-17-launch.png). Side finding, not fixed: clicking repo: dungeon_2d.dsl in ring-tool kills the scene, IllegalArgumentException 'intrinsic triangulation needs triangles, face 0 has 4 sides' from RingTool.adoptGraphRings -> SurfaceGeodesics.over (the ring tool cannot take a quad mesh); unrelated to the menu. F5 feel check by the user still open.

Rework 3 (2026-10-03, continuous trackpad scrolling). DELTA PATH: GLFW glfwSetScrollCallback (LwjglPlatform) -> Scene.setScrollCallback / AutomationInputBinder -> MouseTrap.scrollCallback(double y), which now adds y untruncated to a new double MouseTrap.queuedScrollDelta (replaces int queuedMouseWheelTicks and its (int)(4*y) truncation) -> once per frame OrbitMouseTrap.paintUpdate drains the whole sum: if the scroll region under the cursor claimsWheel() it gets ScrollHandler.onScrollDelta(delta), else the orbit zooms. MouseTrap.ScrollHandler gained two default methods, claimsWheel() (false) and onScrollDelta(double); OrbitMouseTrap.WheelClaimer, onWheelTicks, ROWS_PER_WHEEL_NOTCH and the ease (WHEEL_EASE_NANOS, easeStartOffsetY, easeStartNanos, nanoClock) are removed, so OrbitMouseTrap holds no region type of its own. The orbit no longer decays stale deltas: every delta is applied once. MENU: MenuScrollBox.onScrollDelta moves scrollOffsetY by -delta x PIXELS_PER_SCROLL_UNIT = 90 px immediately, clamped to [0, maximumScrollOffsetY]; 1.0 (a wheel notch) = 3 rows of the 30 px font. No easing: drawnScrollOffsetY() returns scrollOffsetY and is kept with maximumScrollOffsetY for VIEW-16's scroll bar. Direction unchanged: a negative delta (wheel toward the user; a natural-scrolling trackpad swipe up) moves to later rows. ZOOM: the orbit zooms by 0.97^(4 x delta), the same 0.97^4 per 1.0 as before, now for fractions too. The 2D traps (Scene2DMousePanTrap, TradeMouseTrap) sum the float delta and scale their frame-time step by min(1, |delta|), so a wheel notch (and the web's 100-unit deltas) zooms exactly as before and a trackpad zooms in proportion. FlyCamMouseTrap / ThirdPersonCamera.applyZoom take fractional ticks. The automation scroll route, ixdar-cli scroll and automation_routes.json already took a float delta and were left as they were.
MEASURED (ring-tool, model menu open, cursor on the models box, POST /input/scroll one event per frame, ui-state read 2 frames later; log tmp/view17-trackpad-offsets.txt, script tmp/view17_trackpad_probe.py): start 600 (max 600). 50 x +0.05: every event moved the drawn offset exactly -4.5 px (600 -> 595.5 -> 591 ... -> 375.0), visible from the first event. 20 x +0.15: exactly -13.5 px each (375 -> 361.5 ... -> 105.0). 5 x -1.0: exactly +90 px each (105 -> 195 -> 285 -> 375 -> 465 -> 555). 75/75 events had 0.0000 px error against delta x 90. Total motion 945 px = (2.5 + 3.0 + 5.0) x 90 (signs mixed so no event hit the clamp). Rest at 555 px (18.5 rows): the top row is cut at the box edge under MODELS and the bottom row above Recompute (tmp/view17-trackpad-rest-555px.png).
ZOOM (tmp/view17-zoom-distances.txt): cursor off the menu, 20 x +0.05: distance 3.596090 -> 3.574250 after the first event, then 3.183594 after the last; ratio 0.885293, which equals 0.97^4 exactly (tmp/view17-slow-zoom-after.png). 2D (irregular-grid-canvas): 20 x -0.05 zoomed in about 5 % (tmp/view17-2d-before.png, tmp/view17-2d-after-slow-zoom.png); one +1.0 notch took the view back to within 3 % of the start pixels (tmp/view17-2d-after-one-notch-back.png). Before the change, all of these small deltas truncated to 0 ticks and did nothing.
TESTS: ScrollRegionHitTest.trackpadSizedDeltasReachTheRegionUntruncatedOneFrameAtATime (50 x 0.05 through scrollCallback + paintUpdate: 50 deltas of exactly 0.05 summing to 2.5), deltasQueuedBetweenFramesReachTheRegionOnceAsTheirExactSum, aSlowTrackpadZoomOffEveryRegionMovesTheCameraByTheWheelRatePerUnit; MenuScrollBoxWrapTest.everyTrackpadDeltaMovesTheDrawnRowsInProportionAtOnce, theOffsetIsClampedToTheRowsAndAHiddenBoxIgnoresTheWheel, theOffsetRestsAtAnyPixelThroughLayout; the cut-row click test is kept, and the ease tests were removed with the ease. mvn test 385 run, 0 failures; mvn -q compile clean; tools/teavm-build.sh OK (0 errors); ixd wt done view-17 passed (tmp/view-17-launch.png). Open: on the web, WebPlatform passes WheelEvent.deltaY (about 100 per notch, opposite sign) as the delta, so a web menu box jumps to its end per notch and the web orbit zoom is 0.97^400; this was so before as well and is left for a follow-up. The F5 feel check on the trackpad by the user is still open.
